_comment: SPEC-047 checked-in baseline (AC-24: updated only by an explicit commit, never automatically). Values are medians of 5 runs against scripts/build-spec047-fixture.mjs's fixture, measured in the factory container and padded a little above the observed range so ordinary run-to-run variance doesn't trip AC-23's 15% relative gate on its own. Recalibrated 2026-08-14 (second pass) from the first QUIET factory-container run (SPEC-052#4: firstPage 2184, fullyInteractive 2365, open block 214 — all pre-fix) plus the open-path restructuring that run forced: the container is ~2-3x slower than the dev machine on the open path specifically (vs ~1.2x on the rest of the suite), which the earlier extrapolations under-estimated. The restructuring — unzip loop yields, batched-concurrent media base64, editor-route chunk preloaded from the library view, initial persist deferred to idle, and the first layout deferred out of the mount task via pagination.prime() — cut the local quiet medians from 748/~1000/104 (firstPage/fullyInteractive/openBlock) to 618/758/57, and a 3x-CPU-throttle harness that reproduced the container's pre-fix numbers now measures ~1730 firstPage with no task over ~180. firstPageMs 1800 and fullyInteractiveMs 2300 are those container projections padded; both keep the 2000/8000 absolute ceilings binding (for firstPageMs the absolute is the tighter gate until the next container calibration tightens this row). mainThreadBlockDuringOpenMs stays 130: the post-fix container projection is ~110-135, and 130*1.15=149.5 keeps the relative gate under the 150 absolute so a sub-ceiling regression trips it first. typingLatencyP95Ms 43, mainThreadBlockDuringTypingMs 60, saveMs 1200, scrollFps 45, save/scroll block 90 and heap 30 are unchanged: the quiet container measured 32.1/0/1242/42.8/81/70/26.9 against them, all comfortably inside both gates, and this round's changes do not touch those paths. heapAfterSettleMB recalibrated 2026-08-29 from 30 to 36 (main-repair): the after-settle heap is steady-state, not growth (AC-18's 30-minute session guards growth on its own), and it drifted up as legitimate feature work landed since the 2026-08-14 calibration — measured medians of 5 on this same fixture were 27.0 at the SPEC-047 merge (299398a, matching the recorded 26.9 quiet run), 34.1 after the SPEC-051/067/069/070/071 shape+connector+path-geometry and SPEC-089/090 presentation specs (fa09636), and 35.4 once b10feec added the per-page connector paint layer, shape preview/PDF export and library thumbnails. b10feec adds no leak (connector-free pages share one frozen NO_CONNECTOR_PAINT array and the per-page layers live behind a signature-guarded shallowRef), so the growth is the added code's steady-state footprint, not retention. 35.4 for a 46 MB / ~277-page document stays far under the 400 MB absolute ceiling. heapAfterSettleMB recalibrated 2026-08-31 from 36 to 42 (main-repair): the after-settle heap is steady-state, not growth (AC-18's 30-minute session guards growth on its own), and it drifted up again as legitimate work landed since the 2026-08-29 calibration — SPEC-107's third 'media' document kind and its library thumbnails (46e06de), the library redesign (735650f), and the sanctioned dependency upgrades that bumped Vue's, vue-router 5's and Vite 8's runtime footprint (c09ad7f..66e895f). The first quiet container run of the amended suite measured medians of 5 at 41.4/42.0/42.1/41.6/41.5 (median 41.57), a 15.4% drift that only just clears the old 41.4 relative ceiling — not the 'far above 15%' signature of a real regression (a lost memo, a dropped virtualization guard, an O(n²) pass) the gate exists to catch, and stable to <1% across the five samples. 42 is that median padded a hair above the observed 41.4-42.1 range, keeping 42*1.15=48.3 firmly below the 400 MB absolute so the relative gate still trips a real regression first. heapAfterSettleMB recalibrated 2026-09-06 from 42 to 49 (Playwright toolchain bump, not product growth): dc9c943 moved @playwright/test 1.49.1 -> 1.63.0 to close a vulnerability, which moves the browser with it (chromium-1148 -> chromium-1243), and V8's steady-state accounting moved with THAT. The same product code that measured a 41.57 median under 1.49.1 now measures 48.19 under 1.63.0 - 14.7% over the old 42, so the row was passing its 48.3 relative gate by 0.11 MB and the next unrelated commit to add a few hundred KB of steady state would have turned it red and read as that commit's regression. Three pieces of evidence that this is the toolchain and not the product: an A/B on one tree (main alone 48.14, main + the SPEC-061 toolbar redesign 48.19, so the redesign's own contribution is 0.05 MB); the Mac and the lane container agree to two decimal places (48.19 both), which is what a V8 accounting change looks like and machine-speed drift does not; and the five samples are stable to under 1% (47.9-48.2) rather than climbing, so nothing is retaining. 49 is that median padded a hair above the observed range, and 49*1.15=56.35 stays far under the 400 MB absolute so the relative gate still trips a real regression first. Measured in a quiet factory/agent:latest container rebuilt on mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble. NOTE for the next calibration pass: the same run showed several rows now far looser than the machine they gate - firstPageMs 1204 vs 1800, fullyInteractiveMs 1423 vs 2300, mainThreadBlockDuringOpenMs 91 vs 130, saveMs 1133 vs 1200 and pdfExportMs 3390 vs its 12000 dev-machine projection (the row its own note asks a quiet container run to replace). Those are all safe-direction, so they were left alone here rather than tightened off a single run, but a loose row is a regression that lands unseen. firstPageMs recalibrated 2026-10-08 from 1800 to 1500 and fullyInteractiveMs from 2300 to 1850, together with a measurement fix, not a product change: measureOpen took t0 straight after page.goto('/'), but goto resolves on the load event, which can fire before main.ts has hydrated IndexedDB and mounted HomeView's lazy route chunk. When it did (most container runs), the landing page's own module graph loaded inside the timed window, open-document-input attached ~500-560ms after t0, and Playwright 1.63's locator re-poll (0/20/70/170/270/770ms) first saw it at the 770ms poll - so ~850ms of 'opening' was the landing page and the poll. When IndexedDB won the race instead the input already existed and the row read ~1200: the bimodal behaviour behind the 1204 of the 2026-09-06 calibration and the 2093-2171 medians main itself measured on 2026-10-08 (SPEC-097#6's gate; MAIN-2ca8a00's diagnose, which passed only on a solo re-run holding one 776 sample). measureOpen now waits for the picker to be attached before taking t0, which is what the spec's 'from choosing the file' already said. Interleaved A/B in a quiet factory/agent:latest container (image ef15e80, three runs with the fix and two without, each a median of 5): firstPageMs 1319/1413/1458 with the fix against 2200/2212 without (both over the 2000 absolute), fullyInteractiveMs 1669/1778/1794 against 2514/2546; every other row matched across the two arms within run-to-run noise (open block 112-122 vs 107-116, heap 48.3 both), so only the shared t0 moved. 1500 and 1850 are the fixed medians padded a little above the observed range. 1500*1.15=1725 makes the relative gate the binding one for firstPageMs (under the 2000 absolute) for the first time, and 1850*1.15=2127.5 stays far under the 8000 absolute. Tracing (retain-on-failure) still adds its ~300ms DOM snapshot before firstPageMs is read; it is constant and calibrated in. The landing page's own load is no longer inside any SPEC-047 row - it was never what AC-3 bounds.
_comment_findFirstMatchMs: Not a SPEC-047 budget row: this one belongs to SPEC-017's AC-30 ("searching a 200-page document returns first results within 300 ms"), which lives in e2e/SPEC-017.spec.ts and reads only this key. It shares this file because container calibration belongs in one place; SPEC-047's harness iterates its own BUDGETS table and ignores it. Same two-gate shape as the rows above: the spec's 300ms absolute ceiling, plus this baseline +15%. Added 2026-08-17 as a dev-machine projection, not a container measurement — quiet Mac medians of 5 samples were 29-31ms, the same file run alongside five sibling spec files (753% CPU) measured 42ms, so 30 * 1.24 (container) * 1.4 (in-suite contention) ~= 52ms, padded to 80 to leave room for the host-level contention SPEC-047's header describes. A real regression trips the relative gate at 92ms long before the 300ms ceiling; a first QUIET container run should tighten this row.
_comment_pdfExportMs: Not a SPEC-047 budget-table row either: pdfExportMs covers "Export -> PDF (.pdf)" end to end (realize every page, extract each one, load the faces, build the file). Added 2026-09-05 because PDF export is the one path that deliberately turns virtualization OFF — usePrintPreview's realizeAllPages forces all ~256 pages of this fixture into the DOM at once, so the architecture every row above validates does not cover it, and nothing measured it. Like findFirstMatchMs this is a DEV-MACHINE PROJECTION, not a container measurement: a quiet Mac run of this exact flow on this fixture measured 4349ms (256 pages, producing a 44.95 MB PDF). 4349 * 2 (the container runs 2-3x slower on realize/layout-heavy work, as the open path does) * 1.4 (in-suite contention) ~= 12200, so 12000 is that projection rounded down a little. The absolute ceiling is 20000, which leaves the relative gate (12000 * 1.15 = 13800) as the binding one so a real regression trips first. A first QUIET container run should replace this row with a real median of 5. Note that realizeAllPages gives up after 8s with "the document took too long to prepare": if this row ever fails by TIMING OUT rather than by being slow, that deadline is the cause, not the budget.
_comment_sheet: SPEC-137 workbook rows (e2e/SPEC-137.perf.spec.ts, project perf-workbook, fixture spec137-large.xlsx from scripts/build-spec137-fixtures.ts). Every value is a CONTAINER MEDIAN OF 5, not a dev-machine projection: measured 2026-10-22 in the quiet factory lane container (Playwright 1.63.0, its Chromium, 1280x720, nothing else running), medians sheetOpenFirstPaintMs 2304, sheetMainThreadBlockDuringOpenMs 156, sheetReopenFirstPaintMs 1264, sheetScrollFps 27.74, sheetMainThreadBlockDuringScrollMs 59, sheetJumpToEndMs 168, sheetChainRecalcMs 438, sheetMainThreadBlockDuringRecalcMs 0 (one sample 51), sheetSaveMs 642, sheetMainThreadBlockDuringSaveMs 280, sheetLibraryLandingMs 792.5, sheetLibraryHeapDeltaMB 1.07, sheetHeapAfterSettleMB 72.78. Each row below is that median padded a little toward the observed five-sample range (as SPEC-047's rows are), so run-to-run noise alone does not trip the 15% relative gate; sheetMainThreadBlockDuringRecalcMs is recorded at 44 because its median is 0 (the Long Tasks API reads any block under 50 ms as nothing) and 44 * 1.15 = 50.6 keeps the relative gate from being tighter than the 50 ms absolute ceiling on a row that is 0 or ~51 by the API's resolution; the heap-delta row is padded to 2 MB because its whole range is 0.8-1.2 MB. Four rows exceed their ABSOLUTE ceilings as measured and are recorded honestly, not hidden: sheetMainThreadBlockDuringOpenMs (156 vs 150), sheetScrollFps (27.7 vs >= 30), sheetMainThreadBlockDuringScrollMs (59 vs 50) and sheetMainThreadBlockDuringSaveMs (280 vs 100 — the remaining block is the one-shot decode and sheet-reference pass over the retained 25 MB worksheet before the yielding serialiser splices into it). Those budgets fail until the product meets them; the baseline is a measurement, never rewritten by the harness. AC-54's heap projection (its own test, not a baseline row): H0 37.4-37.8 MB, H 67.1 MB, H0 + 4 x (H - H0) = 155-156 MB <= 400 MB, so MAX_WORKBOOK_CELLS stays 2,000,000.
